name: Earth sea level
source_note: Dry air is about 20.9% O2 by volume. Standard sea-level pressure is 1 atm = 101.325 kPa = 14.696 psi (U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976); 14.7 psi is the rounded value.

name: International Space Station
source_note: The ISS cabin is kept close to sea-level air: about 14.7 psi total pressure and about 21% O2. Nominal rounded values; the actual O2 level varies within station limits.

name: Moon base / pressurized rover
source_note: Exploration atmosphere of 34% O2 at 8.0 psi, as set in the FlameMind team brief. Lunar surface gravity is 1.62 m/s², about one sixth of Earth's (NASA Moon Fact Sheet).

name: Moon base upper pressure
source_note: The Flame in Freefall challenge brief cites lunar habitat atmospheres of 30% or more O2 at 10.2 psi or less. This preset is the edge of that range: 30% O2 at 10.2 psi.

name: Spacesuit
source_note: U.S. spacewalk suits run on pure O2 at about 4.3 psi. Suits are worn in microgravity (spacewalks) and on the Moon, so both gravity classes are checked.

name: Mars habitat
source_note: Assumed: no Mars habitat atmosphere has been chosen, so this reuses the Moon base preset (34% O2, 8.0 psi). Mars surface gravity is 3.71 m/s², about 0.38 g (NASA Mars Fact Sheet).
